sentences.text: The genus name Echinochimaera combines the Greek word for 'spiny' with 'chimaera', a type of ancient fish. This creature had a rounded body, large pectoral fins, and two dorsal fins, one of which possessed a movable spine.

Fossils of E. meltoni show extreme sexual dimorphism, with males reaching a maximum length of 15 cm and females only 7 cm. Males of E. meltoni had four pairs of spikes that may have served for defense and sexual identification.
Echinochimaera reached a maximum length of less than 30 cm.
Echinochimaera is considered one of the earliest known chimaeriform fish. E. meltoni was first described by Richard Lund in 1977.
E. snyderi was also described by Richard Lund.

Researchers suggest that the paddle-like tails indicate E. meltoni was likely neither a predator nor a fast swimmer. The body shape, fins, and paddle-like tail indicate that Echinochimaera was a slow swimmer and likely not a predator.
The abundance of immature male fossils combined with significant sexual dimorphism indicates extreme sexual selection in E. meltoni.
Later discoveries of mature specimens suggest E. snyderi reached a larger adult size than E. meltoni.
Echinochimaera is classified within the order Chimaeriformes. Echinochimaera is assigned to the family Echinochimaeridae.
Echinochimaera was an extinct genus of holosteans living in the Lower Carboniferous, approximately 355 million years ago.
The two known species of Echinochimaera lived during the Upper Mississippian (Serpukhovian) stage. The time range for Echinochimaera is the Serpukhovian, from 326.9 to 323.6 million years ago.
